'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[2022 Vinnytsia attacks]]
****[[July 2022 Vinnytsia missile strike]]
*****At least 23 civilians are killed and more than 100 others are injured by three [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile strikes in [[Vinnytsia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-62163071 (BBC News)]
*Spillover of the [[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel|insurgency in the Sahel]]
**At least 12 civilians are killed by [[Islamic extremism|Islamic extremist]] gunmen during an attack against two villages in northern [[Togo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-12-killed-raids-northern-togo-villages-2022-07-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Three civilians and three security forces are killed in an attack by [[militant]]s at a checkpoint near [[Bamako]], [[Mali]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/six-killed-rare-attack-near-malian-capital-2022-07-16 (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Social media]] site [[Twitter]] experiences a global outage lasting for 45 minutes, making it the site's longest outage since 2016. [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2022/jul/14/twitter-experiences-longest-global-outage-in-years (''The Guardian'')]
*Russia enacts a law that requires all companies to comply with the armed forces' orders to provide goods or services and provide overtime or additional work days if necessary. The requirement for a public [[procurement]] procedure for this type of request is abolished. [https://www.rp.pl/gospodarka/art36701001-kreml-wprowadza-specustawe-podporzadkowujaca-gospodarke-wojnie (''Rzeczpospolita'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Over 40 people are missing after a series of floods in [[Virginia]], United States. All are later accounted for. [https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/1640245/us-weather-state-of-emergency-virginia-floods-ont (''Daily Express'')] [https://www.cnn.com/2022/07/14/weather/buchanan-county-virginia-floods-thursday/index.html (BBC News)]
*One person is killed by a magnitude 5.7 [[earthquake]] in [[Ecuador]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/earthquake-shakes-ecuadors-coast-teen-killed-power-line-86860611 (ABC)]
*Three people are killed and two are injured by a [[mudslide]] that hit a school in [[Antioquia Department|Antioquia]], [[Colombia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/mountains-colombia-caribbean-pablo-lopez-medellin-93f590f3b553b7449491c0001e1f99a9 (AP)]
*[[Pinhão (Alijó)|Pinhão]], [[Districts of Portugal|district]] of [[Vila Real]], sets the highest July temperature ever in Portugal, reaching {{cvt|47.0|C|F}}. [https://www.theage.com.au/world/europe/fires-evacuations-and-health-warnings-as-european-temperatures-hit-47-degrees-20220716-p5b21p.html (''The Age'')] [https://www.ipma.pt/pt/media/noticias/news.detail.jsp?f=/pt/media/noticias/textos/Tempo_muito_quente_julho_2022.html (IPMA)]

'''Health and environment'''
*At least 30 [[green sea turtle]]s are found dead off a beach in [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]], [[Japan]], with many having been stabbed in the neck. The green sea turtle is an endangered species. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-62202902 (BBC)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in South Korea]]
**In [[South Korea]], the [[Constitutional Court of Korea|Constitutional Court]] begins deliberations on abolishing the [[Capital punishment|death penalty]] upon an appeal by the [[Catholic Bishops' Conference of Korea]]. South Korea currently has a moratorium on the issue, having not hanged a [[death row]] inmate in the past 25 years. [https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/article/3185189/why-south-koreas-catholic-bishops-want-dormant-death-penalty-be-fully (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[Media freedom in Russia]]
**[[Russian president]] [[Vladimir Putin]] signs a law expanding the definition of "foreign agents" to all organisations deemed by the [[government of Russia|government]] to have fallen under "foreign influence", beginning on December 1. The law permits [[Roskomnadzor]] to block any websites related to a designated entity without a court order, and restricts these entities from receiving state funds and working with children or at state universities. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2022/07/14/putin-signs-expanded-foreign-agents-law-a78298 (''The Moscow Times'')]
*At least 89 people, including 42 civilians, are killed after [[Crime in Haiti|gang]] warfare over the control of the [[Cité Soleil]] neighbourhood began a week ago between the G9 and G-Pèp gangs in [[Port-au-Prince]], [[Haiti]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-62162390 (BBC News)]
*[[Bolivia]]n justice minister [[Iván Lima]] announces that the [[government of Bolivia|government]] will seek more charges against former [[President of Bolivia|president]] [[Jeanine Áñez]] for her alleged role in [[Senkata and Sacaba massacres|massacres]] perpetrated in [[Senkata]] and [[Sacaba]] in 2019. Añez is already serving a 10-year [[sentence (law)|sentence]] on other [[criminal charge|charges]]. [https://www.pagina12.com.ar/437031-bolivia-justicia-ampliara-denuncia-contra-la-expresidenta-je (''Página/12'')]
*Ripudaman Singh Malik, one of the men acquitted in the [[Air India Flight 182]] terrorist bombing, is shot to death in [[Surrey, British Columbia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-62175291 (BBC News)]
*Gunmen open fire inside a nightclub in [[Tegucigalpa]], [[Honduras]], killing four people including Said Lobo, son of former [[President of Honduras|President]] [[Porfirio Lobo Sosa]]. [https://apnews.com/article/honduras-caribbean-biden-cabinet-tegucigalpa-6716a9103cb93c3320b5914a76ab3833 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[July 2022 United Kingdom government crisis|2022 United Kingdom government crisis]]
**[[July 2022 Conservative Party leadership election|2022 Conservative Party leadership election]]
***[[Suella Braverman]] is eliminated from the leadership race in the second round of voting. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/jul/14/suella-braverman-out-of-tory-leadership-race-after-second-round-of-voting (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2022 Sri Lankan protests]]
**[[Gotabaya Rajapaksa]] resigns as [[President of Sri Lanka]] after fleeing to [[Singapore]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-62160227 (BBC News)]
*[[2022 Italian government crisis]]
**[[Mario Draghi]] offers his resignation as [[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] of [[Italy]] after [[Draghi Cabinet|coalition]] partner [[Five Star Movement|Five Star]] withdraws its support. However, [[President of Italy|President]] [[Sergio Mattarella]] refuses to accept the resignation. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-62171284 (BBC News)]
*[[Prime Minister of Estonia]] [[Kaja Kallas]] resigns to form a new coalition government.  [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2022/07/14/estonian-pm-resigns-to-form-new-government (Euronews)]
